summary: Streamed embedding upload reorder in ingest-proxy results in embeddings mismatched to metadata and high rerank latency
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that after migrating to streamed-batch embedding uploads (SDK v1.9.0) their rerank endpoint began returning many null or low-confidence hits and overall rerank latency spiked from ~120ms to 900-2,000ms for affected queries. The problem appears intermittent and correlates with periods of high concurrent upload traffic (50-200 concurrent streams).

Impact:
- Several production routes returning incorrect rerank results (metadata does not match returned top-k ids).
- Increased user-facing latency and error rates for relationship search flows.
- Customer temporarily disabled streaming uploads and reverted to small synchronous batches.

Environment:
- Customer uses Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) in prod-us-east-1 with dedicated-serving tier.
- SDK used: redwood-sdk-python v1.9.0 (streamed upload helper).
- Ingest path: customer -> SDK -> ingest-proxy (k8s) -> embeddings-service -> vector-store (hnsw) -> reranker service.

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Start 100 concurrent streaming upload clients using SDK v1.9.0 with compressed payloads and checksum header X-Embed-Checksum.
2) Each stream uploads a sequence of 1,000 embeddings with associated metadata ids (external_id) as JSONL frames.
3) Immediately perform rerank queries against the same namespace while uploads are in-flight.
4) Observe rerank results and inspect matched IDs and metadata.

Observed behavior:
- Top-k returned IDs sometimes do not match metadata attached to those IDs when queried from the vector-store; e.g., rerank returns doc_id=doc-231 but API metadata for doc-231 corresponds to a different customer record.
- Latency for rerank jumps to 900-2,000ms during upload storms; 5xx rate at ingest-proxy rises from ~0.1% to 2-3% briefly.
- Issue is transient: when uploads slow down, consistency returns.

Expected behavior:
- Streaming uploads should preserve row ordering / id mapping and be visible atomically or in a consistent manner for reranks.
steps_to_reproduce: Start 100 concurrent streaming upload clients using SDK v1.9.0 with X-Embed-Checksum header
Upload JSONL frames (external_id + embedding vector) via streaming helper
Run rerank queries against namespace while uploads are in-flight
Compare top-k ids to metadata queries via GET /vectors/{id} to confirm mapping

comments: 2026-03-01 - Support (Jordan Patel): Initial ticket opened after call with Synaptiq Health. They believe SDK streaming change correlates with regression. Collected request_ids and representative examples; asked for traces and sample payloads.

2026-03-02 - SRE (Maya Chen): Started triage, observed ingest-proxy pod logs showing out-of-order chunk processing under burst. Reproduced partially with internal load test. Created INT-4022 to instrument reorder metrics and locking in ingest-proxy.

2026-03-03 - Engineering (Luca Moretti): Hypothesis: decompress worker pool in ingest-proxy returns processed chunks to aggregator without ordering barrier when concurrency high. Added sequence verification and synthetic test showing 1.8% reorder at 200 concurrent streams.

2026-03-04 - Support (Jordan Patel): Shared temporary workaround with customer: downgrade SDK to synchronous small-batch mode OR gate streaming to 10 concurrent streams. Customer applied gate and reported immediate reduction in bad rerank hits.

2026-03-05 - Engineering (Maya Chen): Patch prepared to add per-stream sequence reordering buffer and checksum validation before writing to embeddings-service. PR: https://github.com/redwood/ingest-proxy/pull/982. Rolling a canary to staging for further validation.
2026-03-05 - Customer (Synaptiq Health): Confirmed that enabling gated concurrency reduced issue incidence; requested ETA for hotfix to move back to full streaming throughput.
investigation_notes: Reproduced with internal harness: configured 180 concurrent streaming clients, observed reorder rate ~1.6-2.1% when worker pool under CPU pressure.

Root cause narrowed to ingest-proxy: decompressor worker threads push completed chunks to aggregator channel without preserving original sequence number, aggregator writes to embeddings-service as received.

Checksum header X-Embed-Checksum sometimes mismatches when chunk arrives out-of-order because per-chunk checksum validated but mapping to external_id is tied to sequence; downstream vector-store writes correct bytes but wrong external_id association is created due to reordering logic.
Reranker subsequently queries by id and retrieves metadata that belonged to a different chunk (observed swap pattern between adjacent chunks).
No corruption of embedding vectors observed; problem strictly mapping/order-related.
resolution_notes: Workaround provided: customer gated concurrency to <=10 streaming clients or switched to SDK v1.8.x synchronous batch path; both reduced incidents.

Hotfix implemented in ingest-proxy: introduce per-stream sequence buffer and apply ordered delivery to embeddings-service; additional validation to reject sequence holes and surface explicit 400s to client when sequence gap detected.
PR merged: https://github.com/redwood/ingest-proxy/pull/982. Canary rollout to staging completed 2026-03-05; load tests show reorder reduced to <0.01% at 200 concurrent streams.

Plan to roll to prod us-east-1 in a staged fashion with canary pods for 2 hours, followed by progressive rollout across replicas. Scheduled prod rollout: 2026-03-07 02:00 UTC with on-call SRE monitoring dashboards and automated rollback on >0.5% reorder metric threshold.

Post-incident actions: update SDK streaming docs to recommend backpressure settings for heavy-concurrency customers, add sequence-reorder dashboards and alerts, and add end-to-end integration test to CI that simulates compressed streaming under CPU pressure.
Customer follow-up: Synaptiq Health requested confirmation once prod rollout completes; assigned CS lead to coordinate.
